title: Boundary Ball Readouts and Linearized Einstein Gravity in a Source–Readout Architecture
sourceMethod: Manual mathematics transcription from the controlling PDF, with independently organized web prose and all substantive proofs and examples. No matching verification supplement was supplied for this paper.

records.sourceSection: Abstract
coverageNotes: Common perturbation, two independent weighted-residual derivations, determining family and radial completion, explicit fixed-frame kernel; equation recovery distinguished from metric reconstruction.

records.sourceSection: 1 Introduction
coverageNotes: Relates the reconstruction to Faulkner et al., source-to-readout, modular transport, horizon thermodynamics and the different nonlinear spin-two derivation. States the first-order, classical and holographic-input scope.

records.sourceSection: 2 Common source and ball projections: geometric class and Ward data
coverageNotes: Poincaré AdS and cosmological constant, residual, radial gauge and finite-boundary regularity, bounded integration domains, trace and conservation conditions, and the limitation on inferring a CFT state from the Ward data.

records.sourceSection: 2 Common source and ball projections: ball boost
coverageNotes: Common tangent and aperture definition, complete bulk Killing generator, conformal boundary limit, hemisphere, surface gravity and positive slice lapse.

records.sourceSection: 2 Common source and ball projections: energy projection
coverageNotes: Stress-tensor normalization and one-sided integral; complementary action of full modular implementer, regulated and continuum formulations, stationarity of relative entropy.

records.sourceSection: 2 Common source and ball projections: area and anchoring
coverageNotes: Complete area variation, induced metric, inverse and volume density, exact radial canonical momentum, fixed-cutoff endpoint, zero time momentum, dimension-dependent sufficient falloff and cancellations.

records.sourceSection: 3 Off-shell charge identity: spatial charge
coverageNotes: Spatial charge in the geometric class; holographic minus spatial energy as boundary trace up to the chosen difference sign, with trace recovery by the small-radius limit. Boundary conservation is used separately.

records.sourceSection: 3 Off-shell charge identity: theorem and defect formula
coverageNotes: Exact equality of normalized spacetime and slice forms, with frame-dependent time-time contraction.

records.sourceSection: 3 Off-shell charge identity: covariant phase-space proof
coverageNotes: Presymplectic potential, Noether charge, full variation at fixed generator, linearized Noether identity, symplectic-current cancellation, bifurcation and asymptotic pullbacks and oriented Stokes theorem.

records.sourceSection: 3 Off-shell charge identity: independent slice proof
coverageNotes: Gauss constraint, full divergence identity and lapse Hessian, hemisphere and cutoff face fluxes, leading coefficient decomposition and agreement of normalizations.

records.sourceSection: 4 From readout data to the local equation: scalar inversion
coverageNotes: Explicit continuous integrand; weighted-to-unweighted derivative; polynomial moment induction with radius and center differentiation, density on the upper hemisphere, and local open-region scope.

records.sourceSection: 4 From readout data to the local equation: determining frames theorem
coverageNotes: Equivalence in the Ward-compatible class; finite frame count and all-slice requirement.

records.sourceSection: 4 From readout data to the local equation: polarization proof
coverageNotes: Common region coverage, explicit spanning family of timelike vectors and pair arithmetic, normalization invariance and genericity by determinant.

records.sourceSection: 4 From readout data to the local equation: radial proof
coverageNotes: Weak linearized Bianchi identity for C² perturbations, both radial equations, exact integrated residual and curvature coefficients, application of trace/conservation and converse.

records.sourceSection: 4 From readout data to the local equation: return maps
coverageNotes: Factorization, injectivity on realized Ward-compatible residuals, one-slice quotient, limited frame-count claim and distinct on-shell metrics with zero defects.

records.sourceSection: 5 Metric perturbations invisible to restricted families: fixed-frame kernel
coverageNotes: Equivalence with vanishing scalar-curvature variation; unconstrained temporal derivatives and quadratic-in-time example. Editorial link to the companion second-order theorem.

records.sourceSection: 5 Metric perturbations invisible to restricted families: compact lapse
coverageNotes: Explicit bump construction, zero charges, static Ricci formula, nonzero mixed residual, covariance-based non-gauge proof and all rest-frame times.

records.sourceSection: 5 Metric perturbations invisible to restricted families: Ward-compatible nonzero data
coverageNotes: Explicit off-diagonal profile, conserved/traceless boundary data, vanishing area and time charge, transverse equation and numerical residual, boosted detection and CFT admissibility limit.

records.sourceSection: 5 Metric perturbations invisible to restricted families: fixed radius and center
coverageNotes: Exact Bessel identity and both proofs cited in source; positive zero and sine oddness examples; allowed nondecay; on-shell cross example with same stress and zero area, and distinction from boundary-trivial gauge.

records.sourceSection: 6 Verification and scope
coverageNotes: Paper’s 149 results categorized into symbolic, negative-control and numerical checks; analytic additions and numerical Bessel illustration; aperture/Ward/first-order scope and infinite-dimensional kernel. No independent replay is claimed.
